evals.prompt: I want to start using bullet journaling for my project. I'm a backend engineer working on a payments service. Can you set it up for me?
evals.expected_output: Should create bujo/ directory structure with index.md, future-log.md, monthly log for current month, and today's daily log. Should use correct templates. Should ask about upcoming deadlines/events before populating the future log and monthly calendar. Should explain the notation system briefly. Should NOT pre-create any collections.

assertions.text: Creates bujo/ with index.md, future-log.md, monthly/ and daily/ subdirectories, and collections/ directory
Files follow the templates from TEMPLATES.md (index with links, monthly with Calendar and Tasks sections, daily with Morning Priorities/Log/End of Day)
Asks the user about upcoming deadlines, events, or milestones before populating the calendar
Briefly explains or references the notation system (task states, events, notes, signifiers)
Does NOT create any collections proactively — the collections/ directory is empty
Adds the monthly log to the index
Uses the actual current date for file names and content

evals.prompt: Log my work today: finished the API refactor for the payments endpoint, had a standup at 9:30am where we discussed the migration timeline, need to review PR #42 from Sarah, need to update the deployment docs, and I had an idea about using event sourcing for the audit trail.
evals.expected_output: Should create today's daily log with proper notation: completed task marked [x], event with (o), open tasks with [ ], and the idea marked with ! signifier. Should distinguish between tasks, events, and notes correctly. Should ask about morning priorities if not already set.

assertions.text: Uses [x] for the completed API refactor and [ ] for open tasks (review PR, update docs)
Uses (o) for the standup event
Uses ! signifier for the event sourcing idea
Creates or updates bujo/daily/YYYY-MM-DD.md with proper template structure
Correctly classifies each item as task, event, or note — does not make everything a task
Appends to the Log section rather than restructuring or rewriting existing content

evals.prompt: Let's do my monthly review. It's the end of the month and I want to migrate to next month.
evals.expected_output: Should scan for all incomplete tasks across daily logs, monthly log, and collections. Should present monthly reflection prompts. Should walk through each incomplete task ONE AT A TIME asking the user to decide: complete, migrate, schedule, move to collection, or drop. Should flag any task migrated 3+ times. Should create next month's log with migrated items. Should update the index.

assertions.text: Scans for incomplete tasks ([ ]) across daily logs, monthly log, and collections
Presents incomplete tasks ONE AT A TIME for the user to decide, not as a batch list
Asks monthly reflection questions (what worked, what didn't, patterns in migration vs completion)
Marks each task in its original location with the appropriate symbol ([>], [<], [~], [x])
Creates next month's monthly log with migrated items and future log entries
Adds the new monthly log to bujo/index.md
Flags any task that has been migrated 3 or more times and investigates why

evals.prompt: I want to plan a 2-week sprint to ship the authentication feature. We need to add OAuth2 support, implement token refresh, add rate limiting to the auth endpoints, and write integration tests.
evals.expected_output: Should ask about the sprint goal (what does done look like). Should break down the high-level items into 1-day granularity tasks collaboratively with the user. Should create a sprint collection using the sprint template. Should add the sprint to the index and monthly calendar.

assertions.text: Asks what the sprint goal is — what does 'done' look like at the end
Breaks the 4 high-level items into smaller tasks at roughly 1-day granularity
Creates a sprint collection using the sprint template (Goal, Duration, Tasks, Progress, Retrospective sections)
Adds the sprint collection to bujo/index.md
Adds sprint start and end dates to the monthly calendar
Collaborates with the user on task breakdown rather than deciding everything autonomously

evals.prompt: Create a collection to track our hiring process for the backend team. We're looking to hire 2 senior engineers and 1 staff engineer.
evals.expected_output: Should ask for a mission statement (one sentence). Should explore scope and type. Should create the collection with appropriate structure. Should add to the index. Should NOT over-design the collection — start minimal.

assertions.text: Asks for a mission statement — what should this collection accomplish
Identifies appropriate collection type (goal-driven or task-driven) based on the hiring context
Asks about scope — what's in and what's out of this collection
Creates bujo/collections/hiring.md (or similar name) with mission, tasks, and notes sections
Adds the collection to bujo/index.md
Does NOT over-design with excessive sections — starts with a minimal structure that can grow
